 Dense Fog Advisory is in effect Fire at Huntsville apartment complex displaces about 15 families 
 About 15 families are without a place to call home after a fire damaged the Governor’s House Apartments Saturday night. By Philip Green Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 1:36 AM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HUNTSVILLE, Ala. ( WAFF ) - About 15 families are without a place to call home after a fire damaged the Governor’s House Apartments Saturday night.
 Cameron Kilgore, a resident of the complex, says he was away from home when he started receiving calls and messages from neighbors telling him the apartment building was on fire.
 “I received text messages and calls from my neighbors. And they’re like, hey, the house is on fire. The house is on fire. But when I finally saw it with my own eyes, I was just lost for words,” Kilgore said.
 Huntsville Fire & Rescue says crews were called to the 16-unit apartment complex around 10:15 p.m. Saturday. Between eight and 10 fire units responded, with smoke and flames visible when firefighters arrived.
 During firefighting efforts, crews encountered problems with the complex’s privately maintained fire hydrant system, which did not function properly.
 No injuries were reported.
 The fire left approximately 15 families displaced. The American Red Cross and apartment management are working to help residents find temporary housing and coordinate available resources.
 For Kilgore, the impact goes beyond the damage to the building. He says many of his neighbors lost the place they called home.
 “They literally... that’s where they laid their head. That’s where they placed their head down at night. And that’s what they called home,” Kilgore said.
 Despite the difficult circumstances, Kilgore says the support from the Huntsville community has meant a lot to him.
 He is asking people to continue checking on the families affected by the fire and making sure they have the help they need.
 “Just continue to reach out to the neighbors and everybody who is also impacted on this and just make sure everybody is in a good position. At the end of the day, because we’re all families. We’re one community,” Kilgore said.
 Huntsville Fire & Rescue says the cause and origin of the fire remain under investigation.
